I don't know why I keep sabotaging myself every time things start going well. It's like I don't deserve good things.

That pattern you're noticing — things starting to go well, then something pulling you back — is really worth exploring. Sometimes we unconsciously recreate familiar discomfort because it feels 'safe,' even when it hurts us. When did 'good things' start feeling dangerous for you? Was there a time when something good was taken away?

I always end up in relationships where I give too much and the other person takes everything. I thought this time would be different.

The fact that you recognized this pattern — that's already significant. What's happening often isn't about who you're choosing. It's about a role that feels familiar and safe, even if it's painful. Being the 'giver' can be a way of feeling needed, of earning love. When do you first remember needing to earn someone's affection?

I get really anxious when people don't reply to my messages quickly. I know it's irrational but I can't stop checking.

Maybe they're pulling away.' That's not irrational. It's your nervous system protecting you from an old wound. Do you know when this anxiety first started?

Shame about your timeline is one of the most painful kinds of comparison — because the clock feels real.
